title: Tropical and Temperate Cyclones

endcard.line: Footage and pictures: CSU/CIRA and NOAA/NESDIS (public domain); NASA (public domain)

segments.say: Both are called cyclones. Both spin around low pressure. But one is born over a warm sea, and the other where warm and cold air collide.

anim.title: A tropical cyclone needs
items: Little change in wind with height

segments.say: A tropical cyclone needs a large sea surface warmer than twenty-seven degrees, the Coriolis force, steady winds with height, and a weak low to start from.
At its centre is the eye, a calm patch of sinking air. Around it is the eye wall, where air spirals up to great heights.
It draws its power from the warm sea. Once it crosses the coast, called landfall, it is cut off from that fuel and weakens.
Temperate cyclones form outside the tropics, along the polar front, where warm and cold air meet. They have clear warm and cold fronts.
Tropical cyclones are fiercer and move from east to west. Temperate ones cover a larger area, move from west to east, and can form over land too.
For GS One, remember four contrasts: where they form, fronts, strength, and the direction they travel.

sources: NCERT Class 11, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, ch. 9 (Atmospheric Circulation and Weather Systems): conditions for tropical cyclones (sea above 27°C, Coriolis force, small variation in vertical wind speed, pre-existing low, upper divergence); eye and eye wall; landfall; tropical cyclones dissipate on reaching land; extra-tropical cyclones form along the polar front with warm and cold fronts, cover a larger area, move west to east; tropical cyclones originate only over seas, have higher wind velocity, move east to west

quiz.q: Which sea-surface temperature does NCERT give for tropical cyclones to form?
quiz.why: A large sea surface warmer than 27°C is the first condition.

quiz.q: Which cyclones have clear warm and cold fronts?
quiz.why: Temperate cyclones form along the polar front, with warm and cold fronts.

quiz.q: What is the calm centre of a tropical cyclone called?
quiz.why: The eye is a calm region of sinking air; the eye wall surrounds it.
